Phototherapy or photochemotherapy may also be useful. Systemic immunosuppressants including aza- thioprine, ciclosporin, and mycophenolate mofetil have been used in resistant disease.1,4,5 Interferon alfa and topi- cal tacrolimus have also been used successfully in a few cases.1 Actinic prurigo is similar to polymorphic light eruption but less common, and is characterised by persistent pruritic papules on areas exposed to sunlight, often with extension to covered areas. Other features include scarring, cheilitis, and eye involvement. It is managed similarly with sun- screens, topical or oral corticosteroids, and phototherapy or photochemotherapy. Thalidomide has been used, but re- lapse frequently occurs when treatment is stopped.1 Solar urticaria is an uncommon condition that can often be managed with sunscreens alone, but non-sedating anti- histamines such as loratadine may also be helpful. Photo- therapy and photochemotherapy have also been used.1 Xeroderma pigmentosum is a rare autosomal recessive condition in which a defective DNA-repair system fails to repair UV-induced DNA damage.6 The skin is hypersensi- tive to sunlight, resulting in serious sunburn after minimal exposure. From a very early age patients start to develop lentigines (sun or liver spots), spotty hypopigmentation, telangiectasias, calloused thickening, atrophy, scabbing, and scarring. Numerous actinic keratoses, precancerous lesions, and malignant neoplasms of the skin (p.672) de- velop in childhood and many patients die before reaching adulthood. Other effects of the disease include motor im- pairment, mental retardation, ocular damage, leukaemia, and dental caries. Management involves strict avoidance of sunlight and use of broad-spectrum sunscreens. There is some evidence that systemic retinoids, such as acitretin and isotretinoin, may be useful in preventing the develop- ment of skin cancers, although adverse effects from long- term use may be of concern. Topical fluorouracil may be 1582 Dermatological Drugs and Sunscreens used on actinic keratoses and malignant skin cancers. A topical preparation containing recombinant T4 endonucle- ase V, a DNA-repair enzyme, is under investigation to re- duce the incidence of actinic keratoses and skin cancers. Other conditions that can be exacerbated by sunlight in- clude the cutaneous porphyrias (p.1448), lupus erythema- tosus (p.1513), and sometimes herpes labialis (p.854). 1. Ferguson J.
